content: Before starting ribavirin and each time you receive a refill, carefully read the medication guide provided by your pharmacist. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically twice daily with food. Swallow the medication whole without crushing or chewing it. For optimal effectiveness, maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body by taking it at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking ribavirin and any other prescribed antiviral medications for the full duration of the treatment, even if your symptoms improve after a short time. Common side effects of ribavirin may include nausea, diarrhea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, difficulty sleeping, cough, reduced appetite, weight changes, dry skin, or alterations in taste or hearing. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to ribavirin are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the United States, you can also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088, and in Canada, to Health Canada. Before taking ribavirin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ribavirin may cause dizziness or blurred vision, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you are confident you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages during treatment. Ribavirin must not be used during pregnancy due to the risk of harm to an unborn baby. Female patients or female partners of male patients should undergo a pregnancy test before starting this medication. Pregnancy tests should continue during treatment and for a period after stopping the medication (9 months for female patients and 6 months for female partners of male patients). If you or your partner becomes pregnant or suspect pregnancy, inform your doctor immediately. It is unknown whether ribavirin passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of ribavirin or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions, so consult your healthcare provider for more information. In the event of an overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While taking ribavirin, your doctor may recommend regular lab and medical tests, such as pregnancy tests, blood counts, liver, thyroid, and heart function tests, EKGs, and eye exams, to monitor your condition and detect any potential side effects. Attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store ribavirin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about ribavirin. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
